thought.text: Everything checks out. Let me do a final confirmation of the ES config (CORS) and the overall state for the report.

reasoning_content:
The chart data matches the ground truth exactly:
- Justin Bieber: 2, Cardi B: 1, Dua Lipa: 1, Ed Sheeran: 1, Megan Thee Stallion: 1, The Kid LAROI: 1, The Weeknd: 1 ✓ (matches the ES aggregation results)

The Komono page loads along with the Leaflet map (as expected — a map example that requires the KOSIS dataset; one 404 resource, probably a data file for the komono index, which is as expected since the dataset hasn't been imported — it's already been documented as "incomplete/unknown" in the summary). This is not a defect of the app; it's just that this particular example lacks a dataset.

All items in the guide have been verified:
1. ✓ Web server (nginx 1.18) — running, serving the app on port 80
2. ✓ Elasticsearch service — 7.17.28 running, green cluster
3. ✓ Folders copied to the document root: config, externalPackages, i18n, src, php, examples + top-level HTML page + top-level data/ folder (all present, confirmed via diff that all source files are deployed)
4. ✓ HTML page works and finds the imported files (all 10 assets in index.html → 200; all 20 app HTML pages → 200)
5. ✓ Configuration adjusted: baseConfig.json points to http://localhost:9200, proxyUrl is null (direct mode)
6. ✓ php proxy works (only needed if the browser can't access ES; verified with the correct protocol)
7. ✓ End-to-end browser verification: the main explorer page lists the indices from ES, loads the mapping, populates the filter dropdown with real data, and executes a search that renders a bar chart of the actual data from the index

The only remaining item is the KOSIS example dataset, which the guide itself notes requires dataset import via the CLI script — the summary also clearly documents this as out-of-scope for the core install, and the `data/` folder the guide mandates for the KOSIS example exists.

Another sanity check: the guide says "copy the HTML pages you want to provide to the same folder on the web server" — done. Also the guide says "adjust the values in the config file used by the HTML page to the correct index name and base URL" — the main page uses a dynamic index selection and a base URL that matches the local ES. Done.

Finally, let me do a last confirmation that the ES and nginx config files exist where they should, and then wrap up. Actually, I have enough evidence. To make the report airtight, let me also quickly verify the ES yml config claim (CORS).
